meta.title: How the Grok Harness Works
meta.subtitle: xAI's terminal agent: tools, sessions, skills, and the loop that ships code

report_card.summary: The Grok Harness is a terminal-based agentic coding system from xAI. A model loop drives tools — file edits, shell, search, subagents, skills — under permission and project rules, with three surfaces: interactive TUI, headless scripts, and ACP for IDEs.

story.title: What Is a Harness?
story.narration: A harness is not the model. It is everything around the model that makes coding possible: a terminal UI, a tool runtime, permissions, session memory, and project rules. Grok Build is xAI's agentic harness — the scaffolding that turns language into file edits and verified shell work.

story.title: Three Ways In
story.narration: You meet the harness three ways. The interactive TUI is the daily driver — scrollback, prompts, and live tool streams. Headless mode runs one prompt for scripts and CI. Agent mode speaks ACP over stdio or WebSocket so IDEs and custom clients can own the session.

story.title: The Tool Loop
story.narration: Every turn is the same loop. You send a prompt. The model reasons, then calls tools: read files, search the repo, run shell, edit code, spawn subagents. Results stream back into context. The model continues until the task is done or you cancel. That loop is the heart of the harness.

story.title: Built-in Superpowers
story.narration: Built-in tools cover the coding surface: filesystem, grep, terminal, web search, GitHub MCP, image and video generation. MCP servers plug in external systems. Sandbox profiles can lock filesystem and network when you need isolation. The harness chooses the tool; you approve the risk.

story.title: Skills and Project Rules
story.narration: Skills are reusable playbooks — a SKILL.md that teaches a repeatable procedure like visualize or vid. Project rules in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md inject local conventions into every session. Hooks run lifecycle scripts. Together they encode how your team works without retyping it every prompt.

story.title: Parallel Minds
story.narration: When work fans out, the harness spawns subagents. Each child gets its own context window, agent type, and optional worktree isolation. Explore, plan, and general-purpose roles run in parallel; the parent keeps only the summary. Context stays sharp because the hard work happens off the main thread.

story.title: Permissions and Trust
story.narration: Autonomy without brakes is chaos. The harness gates destructive and shared-state actions: force push, package downgrades, messages to the outside world. You can auto-approve with care, deny by default, or sandbox the whole run. The model proposes; the harness enforces the boundary you set.

story.title: Memory Across Turns
story.narration: Sessions persist under your home directory. Resume yesterday's work, continue the last chat in this repo, or fork a branch of the conversation. Headless runs can pin session IDs for automation. The harness is not amnesiac — it carries the thread so you can leave and come back.

insights.title: The harness is the product surface
insights.body: Model quality matters, but day-to-day coding speed comes from tools, permissions, skills, and session continuity — the harness layer.

insights.title: One core, three entry points
insights.body: TUI, headless, and ACP share the same tool loop — choose the surface for the job without relearning the agent.

insights.title: Skills encode institutional knowledge
insights.body: A skill turns a multi-step tribal procedure into an invocable package the agent follows without re-prompting.

insights.title: Permissions are part of the architecture
insights.body: Without permission gates and sandboxing, tool-using agents are unsafe by default on shared systems.
